newsitem.title: UK: Safeway up as like-for-like sales impress.
newsitem.headline: Safeway up as like-for-like sales impress.

text.p: Shares in supermarket group Safeway Plc were indicated sharply higher in pre-market trade on Wednesday after the company announced same store sales growth of 3.7 percent in the first six weeks of the current year.
The shares were up 13p at 344p by 0717 GMT.

Safeway reported pre-tax profits before exceptional items of 430 million stg, at the top end of analysts expectations. Underlying profits of 421 million stg were up seven percent over last year and a total dividend of 14.10 pence was up 11 percent year on year.

"The numbers are very reassuring and at the top end of forecasts," said one leading industry analyst, who declined to be named. "The like-for-like performance is well ahead of what people were expecting, some people were thinking that current trading was falling off the cliff, which is clearly not the case."
"The volume picture is very impressive and has been improving throughout the quarter," the analyst said. "This will set the record straight...Safeway is gaining market share."
Like-for-like volume growth remained strong at 4.6 percent, the company said in its results statement.
The analyst maintains his top of the range profit forecast for the current year but expects those analysts who are forecasting little or no growth to upgrade their expectations.
"The shares look ridiculously cheap at these levels," he commented.
